title: selectedCount counts stale ghost columns, so the 'N / total' badge can read e.g. '3 / 3' when only 1 real column is actually selected
description: selectedCount uses `selectedColumns.length` in the explicit (non-all) case, but selectedColumns can include stale names not present in allColumns. The denominator of the badge is `allColumns.length`, which excludes stale entries. The result is a count that double-misleads: the numerator is inflated by ghost columns while the denominator excludes them, so the badge can display the count of selected as equal to or greater than the real total. Example: allColumns=[a,b,c], selected_columns=["a","stale1","stale2"] -> isAllSelected=false, selectedCount=3, badge shows '3 / 3', implying every output column is selected, when in fact only `a` is a real selected output column and b,c are deselected. The count should be the number of selectedColumns that are also in allColumnNames (real, kept columns).
evidence: Line 77: `const selectedCount = isAllSelected ? allColumns.length : selectedColumns.length`. Badge lines 93-95: `{selectedCount} / {allColumns.length}`. staleColumns (lines 28-33) proves selectedColumns can contain names absent from allColumnNames; those are counted by selectedColumns.length but not by allColumns.length.
